hypothesis: H79-H2 (G79-DZD): Unmapped geothermal-conducive fault damage zones in the northwestern Great Basin produce elevated permeability at an optimal cross-fault distance from USGS/INGENIOUS-mapped Quaternary faults. Permeability is concentrated in the damage zone adjacent to fault cores, not on the mapped traces themselves. A distance-decay surface centred on a 200 m optimal damage-zone width, modulated by local fault activity, targets conduits absent from the catalogue because they lie off the mapped traces but within the damage-zone envelope.
mechanism: Single-channel deterministic transform (no ML ensemble): (1) Euclidean distance transform from catalogue fault cells; (2) fault-strike orientation from catalogue gradient; (3) Gaussian damage-zone score centred at 200 m cross-fault distance with 150 m sigma, modulated by fault-activity gradient; (4) zero on catalogue pixels, zero outside the footprint; (5) top-12,000 sparse dots normalised to [0,1]. Written through gems57.submission_writer with format validation. Distinct from G79-THVC: no gravity, magnetics, shallow temperature, sinter, LiDAR scarp or ML ensemble channels.
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene pluvial paleo-shoreline wave-cut benches (Lake Lahontan and Lake Bonneville), fluvial terrace risers along the Humboldt/Carson/Walker rivers, welded ash-flow caldera cooling joints, down-gradient lateral thermal outflow plumes in permeable alluvial fans, and alluvial-fan piedmont slope breaks unrelated to fault damage.
